title: PepBenchmark: A Standardized Benchmark for Peptide Machine Learning
authors: Jiahui Zhang; Rouyi Wang; Kuangqi Zhou; Tianshu Xiao; Lingyan Zhu; Yaosen Min; Yang Wang
why_matters: Defines reusable benchmark and standardized preprocessing/splitting across 29 canonical + 6 non-canonical datasets for peptide ML, directly replacing ad-hoc preprocessing in seed data and validation code.
limitations: Single benchmark snapshot and early preprint; paper-reported results only (no external repo reproducibility logs in abstract).

title: A Standardized Benchmark for Multilabel Antimicrobial Peptide Classification
authors: Sebastian Ojeda et al.
why_matters: Builds ESCAPE (80k peptides, 27 repositories) with cleaner positive/negative separation and hierarchical labels across bacterial/fungal/viral/parasitic activity; strong foundation for dataset construction and label ontology.
limitations: Preprint; public negative/positive split rules and external split strategy details need manual verification in PDF.

title: Prediction of Hemolysis Tendency of Peptides using a Reliable Evaluation Method
authors: Ali Raza; Hafiz Saud Arshad
why_matters: Introduces explicit clustering-based split with <40% similarity guard for train/test to reduce sequence homology leakage in hemolysis classification tasks.
limitations: Outdated pre-deep learning split protocols; details should be revalidated against modern embeddings and updated hemolysis datasets.

title: AmpLyze: A Deep Learning Model for Predicting the Hemolytic Concentration
authors: Peng Qiu; Hanqi Feng; Meng-Chun Zhang; Barnabas Poczos
why_matters: Provides direct sequence-to-HC50 regression with residue-level interpretability via integrated embeddings; useful where current dataset has only toxic/non-toxic labels.
limitations: Cross-study assay harmonization and full dataset provenance are the main uncertainty in direct adoption.

title: HMAMP: Hypervolume-Driven Multi-Objective Antimicrobial Peptides Design
authors: Li Wang; Yiping Li; Xiangzheng Fu; Xiucai Ye; Junfeng Shi; Gary G. Yen; Xiangxiang Zeng
why_matters: Reinforcement-learning hypervolume optimization for jointly balancing activity, hemolysis, and toxicity; practical blueprint for multi-objective objective combinations in generation.
limitations: Likely dataset and scoring details need full-text review to confirm assay unit consistency and false-positive control behavior.

title: MoFormer: Multi-Objective Antimicrobial Peptide Generation Based on Conditional Transformer Joint Multi-modal Fusion Descriptor
authors: Li Wang; Xiangzheng Fu; Jiahao Yang; Xinyi Zhang; Xiucai Ye; Yiping Liu; Tetsuya Sakurai; Xiangxiang Zeng
why_matters: Transformer generator with conditional multi-modal descriptors for simultaneous multi-objective peptide optimization; directly informs score-guided generation and pareto-based ranking.
limitations: Potentially limited to specific benchmark definitions and synthetic splits; validate against your seed schema before merging into pipeline.

title: PepTune: De Novo Generation of Therapeutic Peptides with Multi-Objective-Guided Discrete Diffusion
authors: Sophia Tang; Yinuo Zhang; Pranam Chatterjee
why_matters: Shows practical discrete-space multi-objective control with MCTG guidance (exploration+exploitation) and chemically-modified peptide generation; strong match for design+selection loop.
limitations: Inferred dataset/task setup from abstract; full negative/positive split definitions and computational cost need manual confirmation.

title: Peptide-GPT: Generative Design of Peptides using Generative Pre-trained Transformers and Bio-informatic Supervision
authors: Aayush Shah; Chakradhar Guntuboina; Amir Barati Farimani
why_matters: Provides explicit generation pipeline quality gates (perplexity filtering, convex hull filtering, ESMFold structure checks) and end-task classifers (hemolysis/non-fouling/solubility).
limitations: Abstract-level results only; no full split/label harmonization details in short metadata.

title: Artificial intelligence-driven antimicrobial peptide discovery
authors: Paulina Szymczak; Ewa Szczurek
why_matters: Useful landscape review of discrimination/generation methods and practical controls (positive-only learning, discriminator filtering, latent-space sampling).
limitations: Review breadth is high but depth on raw benchmarks/standards is mixed and may include older/now-outdated baselines.

title: Target-Specific De Novo Peptide Binder Design with DiffPepBuilder
authors: Fanhao Wang; Yuzhe Wang; Laiyi Feng; Changsheng Zhang; Luhua Lai
why_matters: End-to-end target-aware binder generation with synthetic sequence+structure dataset (PepPC-F), useful for binder workflow and manufacturability implications.
limitations: Synthetic dataset assumptions and target selection bias should be checked manually before applying directly to therapeutic use-cases.

title: Full-Atom Peptide Design with Geometric Latent Diffusion
authors: Xiangzhe Kong; Yinjun Jia; Wenbing Huang; Yang Liu
why_matters: Offers full-atom structure-aware generation over binding pockets with shared coordinate transforms; useful for binder quality and cross-target generalization checks.
limitations: Need manual verification on benchmark size and docking/structure scoring assumptions for integration with current target structures.

title: Zero-Shot Cyclic Peptide Design via Composable Geometric Constraints
authors: Dapeng Jiang; Xiangzhe Kong; Jiaqi Han; Mingyu Li; Rui Jiao; Wenbing Huang; Stefano Ermon; Jianzhu Ma; Yang Liu
why_matters: Zero-shot cyclic design from geometric constraints addresses low-data cyclic settings; explicit mention of multiple cyclization strategies and success-rate sensitivity.
limitations: Likely sensitive to backbone and geometry assumptions and downstream chem-synthesis constraints not yet represented in abstract.

title: GeoPep: A geometry-aware masked language model for protein-peptide binding site prediction
authors: Dian Chen; Yunkai Chen; Tong Lin; Sijie Chen; Xiaolin Cheng
why_matters: Sparse-data-friendly transfer from ESM3 for protein-peptide binding site prediction; useful for target-site discovery and failure triage before expensive generation.
limitations: Sparse structural labels and domain-generalization may be fragile for uncommon folds; inspect calibration before hard gating.

title: AutoBinder Agent: An MCP-Based Agent for End-to-End Protein Binder Design
authors: Fukang Ge; Jiarui Zhu; Linjie Zhang; Haowen Xiao; Xiangcheng Bao; Fangnan Xie; Danyang Chen; Yanrui Lu; Yuting Wang; Ziqian Guan; Lin Gu; Jinhao Bi; Yingying Zhu
why_matters: Practical MCP-orchestrated architecture integrating structure-design tools and LLM planning, directly relevant to your agent specs.
limitations: Needs manual validation for failure recovery paths, reproducibility of MCP tool responses, and cost controls when invoking structure tools.

title: MAC-AMP: A Closed-Loop Multi-Agent Collaboration System for Multi-Objective Antimicrobial Peptide Design
authors: Gen Zhou; Sugitha Janarthanan; Lianghong Chen; Pingzhao Hu
why_matters: Closed-loop multi-agent framework with simulated peer-review and multi-objective scoring, matching design-make-test-learn requirements and AMP failure analysis.
limitations: Need full-method appendix for exact reward and split protocols before coding production constraints.

title: From AI for Science to Agentic Science: A Survey on Autonomous Scientific Discovery
authors: Jiaqi Wei et al.
why_matters: Survey with explicit capability map and workflow stages for autonomous research systems, helping define agent contracts and governance.
limitations: General survey scope; translation into peptide-specific protocol still required.

title: Autonomous Agents for Scientific Discovery: Orchestrating Scientists
authors: included
why_matters: useful_next
limitations: module_8,module_7
column13: Taxonomy of agent roles and orchestration patterns useful for designing resilient scientific workflows and human-fallback points.
column14: Literature-wide examples, limited quantitative comparison for wet-lab science stacks.

title: AutoResearchBench: Benchmarking AI Agents on Complex Scientific Literature Discovery
authors: Lei Xiong et al.
why_matters: Benchmarks deep research and wide-research retrieval with clearly named failure modes, useful baseline for literature-agent acceptance criteria.
limitations: Literature-only benchmark; does not validate wet-lab or peptide-generation quality directly.

title: MCP-Cosmos: World Model-Augmented Agents for Complex Task Execution in MCP Environments
authors: Giridhar Ganapavarapu; Dhaval Patel
why_matters: World-model-augmented MCP execution loops improve reliability of tool-driven agents; useful pattern for binder and pipeline orchestrators.
limitations: Task transfer risk from general MCP tasks to peptide workflows; needs domain-specific constraints tests.

title: The AI Scientist-v2: Workshop-Level Automated Scientific Discovery via Agentic Tree Search
authors: Yutaro Yamada et al.
why_matters: Concrete end-to-end design-test-evaluate flow with execution planning and tree-search controls, usable skeleton for DMTL orchestration.
limitations: Domain gap: paper-level automation emphasis requires adaptation for assay and peptide safety controls.

title: Why LLMs Aren't Scientists Yet: Failure Modes
authors: useful_next
why_matters: module_7,module_8,module_3
limitations: Sasha Saito; Emily R. Smith; Kenji Tanaka
column12: Explicit failure-mode taxonomy for autonomous scientific workflows; directly maps into failure ontology and red-team scoring.
column13: Preprint with limited peer review; treat failure frequencies and examples as calibration hints only.
